title: The power of books
paragraphs: For many of us, there’s nothing better than burying our head in a good book. Whether it’s a gripping crime story or a biography of someone’s amazing life, it’s good to read a book to switch off from the distractions of everyday life and help us relax. Maybe that’s why some of them are actually being prescribed as a remedy to sickness.

It may seem obvious that reading is good for us. It can be educational, and, as some say, it can ‘broaden the mind’. A good novel can make us happy or sad, or make us cry as we empathise with characters. The power of books was recognised a few years ago by the British charity Reading Agency, who published a list of books that doctors could offer to patients, tackling topics from depression to dementia to chronic pain. It called this ‘bibliotherapy’ and it’s become so successful that it's about to be extended to children as well.

Professor Philip Davis studies the effects of literature at Liverpool University and is author of a book called Reading for Life. He studies people in reading groups and found that it’s reading literature – written work thought to have artistic merit, that has the best effect. He told the BBC that when reading something for pleasure, “…the brain begins to work from different parts, from a different hemisphere and it gets excited, it gets pre-emotional – and you can see the brain coming to life.”

Of course, it’s easy in our smartphone generation to ditch a good book and fiddle with our phones instead. But opening up a paperback could be a simple way to help boost or maintain our mental health. It's thought they can help you set targets and find focus. And they may allow you to see that awkward situation you've been anxious about for weeks from someone else's perspective.

If you’re not an avid reader it can be hard to know where to begin. If the Reading Agency book list doesn’t appeal, you could to read book reviews, visit a library or bookshop or ask a friend. Once you’ve found the right text, you’ll be hooked! And if you still love your technology, you could always use an e-reader.

vocabulary.entry: gripping /ˈɡrɪpɪŋ/ adj. 扣人心弦的；引人入胜的
vocabulary.example: The film tells a gripping story about a detective's adventure.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影讲述了一个关于侦探历险的扣人心弦的故事。

vocabulary.entry: biography /baɪˈɒɡrəfi/ n. 传记
vocabulary.example: She wrote a biography of her favourite writer.
vocabulary.translation: 她写了一本关于自己最喜爱作家的传记。

vocabulary.entry: switch off /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 不再关注；把注意力从……移开
vocabulary.example: I like to switch off from work when I get home.
vocabulary.translation: 我到家后就喜欢不再想工作上的事。

vocabulary.entry: distraction /dɪˈstrækʃn/ n. 使人分心的事物；干扰
vocabulary.example: Noise from the street is a distraction when I'm studying.
vocabulary.translation: 街上的噪音在我学习时会成为干扰。

vocabulary.entry: prescribe /prɪˈskraɪb/ v. 推荐；开（药）
vocabulary.example: The doctor prescribed some medicine for my cold.
vocabulary.translation: 医生给我开了一些治感冒的药。

vocabulary.entry: remedy /ˈremədi/ n. 疗法；治疗
vocabulary.example: Walking outdoors is a good remedy for stress.
vocabulary.translation: 户外散步是缓解压力的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: broaden the mind /ˈbrɔːdn ðə maɪnd/ 开阔眼界；拓宽思路
vocabulary.example: Travelling to different countries can broaden the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 去不同的国家旅行能开阔眼界。

vocabulary.entry: empathise /ˈempəθaɪz/ v. 共情；同感
vocabulary.example: I can empathise with her because I've had a similar experience.
vocabulary.translation: 我能和她共情，因为我有过类似的经历。

vocabulary.entry: charity /ˈtʃærəti/ n. 慈善机构；慈善团体
vocabulary.example: The charity provides food for homeless people.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的人提供食物。

vocabulary.entry: dementia /dɪˈmenʃə/ n. 痴呆症
vocabulary.example: The old man was diagnosed with dementia last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老人去年被诊断出患有痴呆症。

vocabulary.entry: chronic pain /ˈkrɒnɪk peɪn/ 慢性疼痛
vocabulary.example: He has been suffering from chronic pain in his back for years.
vocabulary.translation: 他的背部慢性疼痛已经持续好几年了。

vocabulary.entry: bibliotherapy /ˌbɪbliəʊˈθerəpi/ n. 阅读疗法
vocabulary.example: Bibliotherapy is used to help some patients with mental health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读疗法被用于帮助一些有心理健康问题的患者。

vocabulary.entry: literature /ˈlɪtrətʃə/ n. 文学作品；文学
vocabulary.example: He studied English literature at university.
vocabulary.translation: 他在大学里学习英国文学。

vocabulary.entry: artistic merit /ɑːˈtɪstɪk ˈmerɪt/ 艺术价值
vocabulary.example: The painting is judged to have great artistic merit.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画被认为具有很高的艺术价值。

vocabulary.entry: hemisphere /ˈhemɪsfɪə/ n. （大脑的）半球
vocabulary.example: The left hemisphere of the brain is responsible for language in most people.
vocabulary.translation: 对大多数人来说，大脑左半球负责语言功能。

vocabulary.entry: ditch /dɪtʃ/ v. 丢弃；抛弃
vocabulary.example: He decided to ditch his old car and buy a new one.
vocabulary.translation: 他决定扔掉旧车，买一辆新的。

vocabulary.entry: fiddle with /ˈfɪdl wɪð/ 摆弄；拨弄
vocabulary.example: She likes to fiddle with her hair when she's nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 她紧张的时候就喜欢摆弄头发。

vocabulary.entry: paperback /ˈpeɪpəbæk/ n. 平装书
vocabulary.example: I prefer paperbacks because they are lighter to carry.
vocabulary.translation: 我更喜欢平装书，因为它们拿起来更轻便。

vocabulary.entry: boost /buːst/ v. 促进；提高
vocabulary.example: Exercise can boost your energy levels and improve your mood.
vocabulary.translation: 运动能提升你的精力，改善你的情绪。

vocabulary.entry: awkward /ˈɔːkwəd/ adj. 令人尴尬的；棘手的
vocabulary.example: It was an awkward situation when we met our ex-friend in the street.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在街上遇到以前的朋友，场面很尴尬。

vocabulary.entry: avid /ˈævɪd/ adj. 热衷的；酷爱……的
vocabulary.example: She is an avid reader who finishes a book every week.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个热衷阅读的人，每周都能读完一本书。

vocabulary.entry: hooked /hʊkt/ adj. 着迷的；入迷的
vocabulary.example: He got hooked on playing chess after his grandfather taught him.
vocabulary.translation: 爷爷教他下棋后，他就迷上了这项运动。

sentences.english: For many of us, there’s nothing better than burying our head in a good book.
sentences.chinese: 对我们很多人来说，没有什么比埋头读一本好书更惬意的事了。

sentences.english: Whether it’s a gripping crime story or a biography of someone’s amazing life, it’s good to read a book to switch off from the distractions of everyday life and help us relax.
sentences.chinese: 不管是扣人心弦的犯罪小说，还是记录某人传奇一生的传记，捧起一本书，暂时抛开日常生活的纷扰，让我们放松身心。

sentences.english: Maybe that’s why some of them are actually being prescribed as a remedy to sickness.
sentences.chinese: 或许正因如此，有些书甚至被当作治疗疾病的药方。

sentences.english: It may seem obvious that reading is good for us.
sentences.chinese: 阅读对我们有益，这似乎是显而易见的事实。

sentences.english: It can be educational, and, as some say, it can ‘broaden the mind’.
sentences.chinese: 阅读有教育意义，而且正如有些人所说，它还能“开阔眼界”。

sentences.english: A good novel can make us happy or sad, or make us cry as we empathise with characters.
sentences.chinese: 一本好小说能让我们或喜或悲，能让我们因共情书中人物而潸然泪下。

sentences.english: The power of books was recognised a few years ago by the British charity Reading Agency, who published a list of books that doctors could offer to patients, tackling topics from depression to dementia to chronic pain.
sentences.chinese: 几年前，英国慈善机构“阅读社”就意识到了书籍的力量，该机构发布了一份书单，医生可以将这些书推荐给患者，内容涵盖抑郁症、痴呆症、慢性疼痛等多个主题。

sentences.english: It called this ‘bibliotherapy’ and it’s become so successful that it's about to be extended to children as well.
sentences.chinese: 这种疗法被称为“阅读疗法”，如今它大获成功，即将推广到儿童群体中。

sentences.english: Professor Philip Davis studies the effects of literature at Liverpool University and is author of a book called Reading for Life.
sentences.chinese: 菲利普·戴维斯教授在利物浦大学研究文学的影响，他还是《终身阅读》一书的作者。

sentences.english: He studies people in reading groups and found that it’s reading literature – written work thought to have artistic merit, that has the best effect.
sentences.chinese: 他对读书小组的成员进行研究后发现，阅读文学作品——那些被认为具有艺术价值的书面作品，能带来最佳效果。

sentences.english: He told the BBC that when reading something for pleasure, “…the brain begins to work from different parts, from a different hemisphere and it gets excited, it gets pre-emotional – and you can see the brain coming to life.”
sentences.chinese: 他在接受BBC采访时表示，当人们为了消遣而阅读时，“大脑的不同区域、不同半球都会开始运作，大脑会变得兴奋，产生前置情绪反应——你能看到大脑焕发出活力。”

sentences.english: Of course, it’s easy in our smartphone generation to ditch a good book and fiddle with our phones instead.
sentences.chinese: 当然，在这个智能手机时代，人们很容易丢下好书，转而摆弄手机。

sentences.english: But opening up a paperback could be a simple way to help boost or maintain our mental health.
sentences.chinese: 但翻开一本平装书，或许是提升或维持心理健康的一个简单方法。

sentences.english: It's thought they can help you set targets and find focus. And they may allow you to see that awkward situation you've been anxious about for weeks from someone else's perspective.
sentences.chinese: 据说读书能帮助人们设定目标、找到专注力，还能让你从别人的视角，看待那件困扰了你好几周的尴尬事。

sentences.english: If you’re not an avid reader it can be hard to know where to begin.
sentences.chinese: 如果你不是一名热衷阅读的人，可能会不知道从何入手。

sentences.english: If the Reading Agency book list doesn’t appeal, you could to read book reviews, visit a library or bookshop or ask a friend.
sentences.chinese: 要是“阅读社”的书单不合你意，你可以读读书评、逛逛图书馆或书店，或是问问朋友的建议。

sentences.english: Once you’ve found the right text, you’ll be hooked!
sentences.chinese: 一旦找到适合自己的书，你就会爱不释手！

sentences.english: And if you still love your technology, you could always use an e-reader.
sentences.chinese: 而如果你依旧钟情于电子产品，也完全可以用电子阅读器来阅读。
